intro.text: Built from the [Technical Design Spec (TDS) — Template](https://app.notion.com/p/406128b264948158a47ffc6690c30962). This is the worked example for other projects. Behaviour is defined in [User Stories](https://app.notion.com/p/405128b2649480a1951cf018caeb9def); this document defines how it's built.

blocks.text: Partner Packs let a client organisation buy a block of points that its employees spend on Scentia short courses. Today there's no self-service: employees find a course in the public catalogue and email Scentia to book, coordinators enrol them by hand, and premium and qualification pack reports are built by combining Salesforce and Moodle CSV exports for each client. Support queries land in the public programs queue or with account managers.

The portal gives employees self-service booking within their contract, gives client administrators approvals, employee lists, usage reporting and renewals, and gives Scentia's two PP coordinators one view across all clients. Salesforce remains the system of record for clients, contracts, courses, offerings and enrolments.

items: **Places and points are rechecked atomically** on submit, approve and change, while Salesforce also sells places through other channels (Book, Approve, Change stories).
**Contract selection rule**: whitelist contract first, then the contract that ends soonest, falling through on insufficient points or out-of-term dates (stories 3.5 AC 2, 4.2 AC 13).
**10-business-day rule** decides whether points are returned or consumed, and whether changes are allowed.

**Holds and auto-expiry**: a pending request holds a place and its points (shown as "pending") for one month, until 10 business days before the start, or until the contract ends, whichever is soonest; reminders at 3 days, end of week, then weekly.
**Approve from email without signing in**, with single-use, expiring, request-bound links.
**Immutable points ledger and activity history**.
**Strict tenant isolation**: admins see only their organisation; internal users see all, view-only for bookings.

**Hourly refresh, live availability**: Salesforce data is refreshed every hour on the hour and the portal shows no freshness timestamps. Availability can't be batch processed, so places remaining are read live from Salesforce at submit, approve and change (stories §2).
**Large exports run in the background** and are delivered when ready.
**Salesforce API budget** is already about 50% used daily (Salesforce Queries meeting).

rows: Same; course list < 500 ms with 500 courses

Salesforce is the system of record for clients, contracts, courses, offerings, enrolments and renewal status. Salesforce's data model allows only one-to-one relationships for client admins, so client admins beyond the primary live in the portal.
Salesforce daily API limit is shared with other integrations and already about half used.

An integration user and External Client App can be created at no licence cost (Salesforce Queries meeting).
The integration user can read an offering's live places remaining through the REST API, and run SOQL delta queries on SystemModstamp for each mirrored object.
Qualification progress is available in Salesforce (Q6).

blocks.text: One Worker serves all three portals, the webhooks, the queue consumers and the crons (ADR-009). Route groups enforce role separation; they share one domain model and one database. Staging and production each run this whole set as separate resources (3.5, ADR-011): they share only the Cloudflare account, the Sentry project and the Supabase project "AIM Partner Packs" (`wyydvkvewxsjryutrpaa`, Sydney). Each environment's database is its own branch of that project, a separate Postgres instance with its own credentials and no shared data; both environments' export files are in the `main` branch's Storage (ADR-013).

blocks.text: `wrangler.jsonc` holds no secrets. Every variable is listed in `.env.example` with a comment. Deployed values are Worker secrets, set separately on each Worker from local, gitignored files (`wrangler secret bulk .env.staging --env staging`, `wrangler secret bulk .env.production`), and they persist across deploys. Locally they come from `.env`, which is symlinked into every worktree. gitleaks runs on pre-commit, pre-push and in CI, with GitHub push protection on.

blocks.title: From merge to customers

items: **Deploy** is Cloudflare Workers Builds, one connection per Worker (3.5). It builds and deploys on every push to that Worker's branch; nothing else deploys. The Cloudflare Vite plugin picks the environment at build time (`CLOUDFLARE_ENV`), so `wrangler deploy --env` has no effect.
**GitHub Actions** only checks (`ci`, 15) and never deploys. Branch rules make a green `ci` a precondition of every merge into `main` and `production` (5.5).
**Migrations are not part of the deploy.** They're run by hand against each environment's database before or straight after the code that needs them reaches it (6.5).

**Manual deploys** are rare and need `wrangler login` on the team account: `CLOUDFLARE_ENV=staging pnpm run build && npx wrangler deploy` for staging, `pnpm run build && npx wrangler deploy` for production.
**First deploy of an environment:** create its queues and DLQs (`wrangler queues create`), migrate its database, set its secrets; KV namespaces are provisioned on first deploy.

blocks.text: Rollback

Roll a Worker back to its previous version from the dashboard (Deployments) or with `wrangler rollback`; the next build from its branch replaces it, so follow up with a revert PR into `main` (and a release, for production). Migrations are expand-and-contract, so the previous version still runs against the current schema and the database is never rolled back. Staging only: before deploying a version from before masquerade (PR #8), end every masquerade session (docs/DEPLOY.md), or the old code treats one as an ordinary session.

Repository `Scentia-How-We-Work/aim-partner-packs`, production tier, solo team (`.scentia.json`). Rules come from Scentia-How-We-Work org rulesets, applied by `/scentia:protect-repo`; the repo has no branch protection of its own.

rows: Staging; the integration branch every PR targets
PR, squash merge (title becomes the commit), branch deleted on merge

Release PR from `main` or `release/*`, or a `hotfix/*` PR; merge commit only

"Protect production branch" ruleset: PR and `ci` required, not strict (it holds merge commits `main` never has), no force-push or deletion. CI rejects heads whose commits aren't on `main`, except `hotfix/*`

blocks.text: Merges, approvals and pushes to `main` or `production` are made by the dev on GitHub, never by Claude Code. Nobody bypasses git hooks (`--no-verify`, `LEFTHOOK=0`).
Every change follows the Scentia worktree workflow, driven by the `scentia` Claude Code plugin, which also injects the team standards at session start from `.scentia.json`.

items: **Start** (`/scentia:start-work`): find or create the Notion ticket, move it to In Progress and assign it (5.9); create `worktrees/<branch>` from `origin/main`, symlink `.env` and `.dev.vars` from the root, run `pnpm install`, and record the ticket in `git config branch.<branch>.notionTask`.

**Build**: read `docs/SPEC.md` first and update it in the same PR. Business rules go in `src/lib` with the failing test first (TDD), I/O in `src/server`. Customer-facing journeys get Playwright e2e tests with an axe WCAG 2.2 AA scan in the same PR. Stryker mutation testing on rules-heavy `src/lib`. Tick each acceptance criterion on the ticket when it's built and tested.
**Try it** (`/scentia:integrate-testing`): merge the branch into the local `testing` branch in the root checkout, which `pnpm dev` serves, to test it alongside other unmerged work.

**Finish** (`/scentia:finish-work`): run `pnpm format:check && pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build`, push, and open a PR into `main` with `Closes <ticket URL>` on the first line and the PR template filled in; set the ticket's `PR Link`.
**Review** (`/scentia:address-review`): fix review comments in the worktree, push, and reply to each; the reviewer resolves threads.

**Merge**: the dev squash-merges once `ci` passes. Workers Builds deploys `main` to staging. If the PR added `drizzle/` migrations, the dev migrates staging (6.5). The ticket moves to Testing/QA. Then `/scentia:finish-work` removes the worktree and local branch and rebuilds `testing` from `main`.

rows: Everything in 15's CI row; required on `main` and `production`

blocks.text: `production` changes only through `/scentia:release`, once QA has passed on staging. Nothing reaches customers on merge to `main`.

items: List what's on `main` but not on `production` (`git log --first-parent origin/production..origin/main`): one squash commit per PR.

For each PR, find its Notion ticket and status. Tickets still In Progress or Testing/QA haven't passed QA. A PR that adds or redesigns a journey also needs the dev's manual accessibility pass on staging (keyboard alone and a screen reader).
Choose the head: `main` if everything passed; a `release/<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch pushed at the last commit before the first untested one; or nothing yet.

Open `Release <YYYY-MM-DD>` into `production`, listing each PR and its ticket. CI's "Promote only commits already on main" step fails any head that isn't an ancestor of `origin/main` (bar `hotfix/*`).
If the release includes migrations, migrate production first (6.5).
The dev merges with a merge commit (the only method `production` allows). Workers Builds deploys the production Worker.
Each ticket the release closed moves to On Production and its developer is removed from `Assignee`; `Part of` tickets stay as they are.

blocks.text: Hotfixes

Only when production needs a fix now and `main` holds untested work, and only with the dev's say-so. Start `hotfix/<name>` from `origin/production`, PR it into `production` (rebased onto `production`, never `main`) and merge with a merge commit; then push the same branch again and PR it into `main`, squash-merged as usual. `production` is never merged into `main`. The ticket moves to On Production when the `production` PR merges.

`/scentia:promote-to-prod` is the standard procedure that takes a Scentia app from the POC tier (one Worker, `main` deploys to customers) to this setup. Its "Staging and production" steps are also how a production-tier app without a `production` branch gets one. For this app, the end state is what 3.5 and 5.5 describe.

rows: SPEC current, `src/lib` unit tests passing their coverage thresholds, open PRs merged first

`scaffold.mjs apply --tier production`: Playwright e2e and axe in CI, `env.staging` in `wrangler.jsonc` with every binding repeated for staging resources, production rules in `.scentia.json`, the production `docs/DEPLOY.md`
Playwright tests for each main journey in SPEC, each ending in an axe WCAG 2.2 AA scan

blocks.text: The order in step 6 matters: the production Worker is moved off `main` before staging is connected to it, so untested work never reaches customers in between.

Work is tracked in the Notion roadmap, not GitHub issues: Projects → Epics → Tickets. This app's project is [Partner Packs Portal](https://app.notion.com/p/408128b2649481fbaed3e6bcaf0e043d) (`notion` in `.scentia.json`); chores go in its Maintenance epic. Each ticket's "User stories" checklist holds its acceptance criteria, ticked when dev done (built and tested). Every PR closes one ticket (`Closes <ticket URL>`, or `Part of` when it delivers only part of it), and the branch records its ticket in git config. The plugin's skills move tickets through the Notion MCP tools.

blocks.text: Drizzle migrations in `drizzle/` (`pnpm db:generate`), expand-and-contract so the previous Worker version always runs against the new schema, reviewed in the PR. CI applies every migration to an empty Postgres 17 database on each run.

Deploys don't run migrations: Workers Builds deploys code only. After a merge that adds `drizzle/` files, the dev runs `DATABASE_URL=<session pooler URL> pnpm db:migrate` against staging, and against production as part of the release (5.7). A missed migration shows as "column … does not exist" errors on that Worker (seen on staging, 02/11/2026). See R8 and Q19.

items: Use the session pooler connection string of the branch being migrated (`staging` or `main`; each has its own ref and password): the direct `db.<ref>.supabase.co` host is IPv6-only.

Never migrate a shared database from an unmerged branch. Drizzle applies only migrations newer than the last one recorded, so a migration renumbered on rebase can leave others silently skipped (seen on staging, 02/11/2026).
A wrong password in a Hyperdrive config makes Supabase ban Cloudflare's egress IPs; fix the password before lifting the ban (14.3).
